A. Blue Ghost Mission 1, sunset of 16 March 2025 (site 18.562 N 61.81 E)
   Published (Firefly press release): "346 hours of daylight", "operating just over 5 hours into the lunar night with the final
   data received around 6:15 pm CDT on March 16". Read as: night began around 18:15-18:35 UTC, to a few tens of minutes;
   the release does not say whether "sunset" is first contact, last limb or loss of power.
   Smooth sphere, no terrain (Horizons only): first contact with the horizontal 03-16 19:37, half 03-16 20:10, last limb 03-16 20:44 UTC

   eye height | independent (Horizons + own skyline)            | app 375f816                     | app 4f007f1
              | skyline cuts   half hidden   last limb           | cuts     half     last limb | cuts     half     last limb
     0.5 m    | 18:09  18:42  19:16:07 (16 Mar)    | 18:11  18:44  19:16:26 (+0.3 min) | 18:11  18:44  19:16:19 (+0.2 min)
     2.0 m    | 18:23  18:56  19:30:03 (16 Mar)    | 18:25  18:58  19:30:19 (+0.3 min) | 18:25  18:58  19:30:11 (+0.1 min)
              the skyline at the setting Sun (azimuth 269.9) is 0.592 deg, formed by ground 768 m away at -3641.1 m (site -3651.2 m)
     5.0 m    | 18:51  19:24  19:57:57 (16 Mar)    | 18:53  19:26  19:58:11 (+0.2 min) | 18:53  19:25  19:58:04 (+0.1 min)
   The app's series is sampled every minute, so its "cuts" and "half" columns are whole minutes.

B. The 14 March 2025 eclipse seen from the Blue Ghost site (Earth in front of the Sun)
   Published (KUT, citing Firefly; times read as CDT = UTC-5): eclipse "starting at 12 a.m." = 05:00, "ending around 4:52 a.m." = 09:52;
   "Totality lasted just over 2 hours, beginning at 1:18 a.m." = 06:18; image "around 3:30 a.m." = 08:30 "as the sun prepared to emerge from totality".
   Independent (Horizons, geometric discs): Earth's limb first touches the Sun 05:00:43, Sun wholly covered 06:17:24 .. 08:34:25 (137 min), last contact 09:51:10 UTC
   App 375f816: first sample with the Sun partly covered 05:01, wholly covered 06:18 .. 08:34 (dark interval 06:17:19 .. 08:34:19), last partly covered sample 09:51
   App 4f007f1: first sample with the Sun partly covered 05:01, wholly covered 06:18 .. 08:34 (dark interval 06:17:19 .. 08:34:19), last partly covered sample 09:51
   Published minus independent: start -0.7 min, totality start +0.6 min, end +0.8 min; the "around 3:30" image is 4 min before the Sun re-emerges.
   Earth's atmosphere is ignored on all sides here: discs are geometric (Horizons uses Earth's equatorial radius).

C. Chandrayaan-3 (69.3741 S 32.32 E): end of the lunar day and the next sunrise, September 2023
   Published: "the Sun would set at Shivshakti point on September 4" (Interesting Engineering); ISRO, 2 Sept: "the next sunrise expected on
   September 22, 2023"; ISRO page, 4 Sept: "Awaiting their awakening around September 22, 2023". Dates only.
   Independent (2 m): skyline starts to cut the Sun 09-04 04:53, last limb gone 09-04 08:02:23; first limb back 09-19 23:57:08, whole disc clear 09-20 02:42 UTC
   App 375f816: sunset 09-04 08:09:01 (+6.6 min), sunrise 09-19 23:56:31 (-0.6 min)
   App 4f007f1: sunset 09-04 08:02:08 (-0.2 min), sunrise 09-19 23:56:40 (-0.5 min)
   Sun at 2023-09-21T18:30 (= 22 Sept 00:00 IST): 8.2 deg above the horizontal, 6.8 deg above the skyline
   Sun at 2023-09-22T18:30 (= 23 Sept 00:00 IST): 11.9 deg above the horizontal, 10.7 deg above the skyline
   So the sunset date agrees (4 Sept, both UTC and IST). The first sunlight computed here falls at 09-19 23:57 UTC = 09-20 05:27 IST, two days
   before the date ISRO gave for "the next sunrise"; through 22 Sept IST the Sun climbs from about 8 to 12 deg. ISRO's date may mean usable power rather than first light: not resolved here.

D. Apollo 15 (26.13239 N 3.6333 E): no published sunset time was found; independent recomputation only
   Independent (2 m): last limb gone 08-13 11:36:55 UTC; eclipse of 6 August 1971 at the site: 17:30:32, total 18:26:23 .. 21:03:21, ends 21:59:08
   App 375f816: sunset 08-13 11:37:01 (+0.1 min); Sun wholly covered 18:26:23 .. 21:03:25 (+0 s, +4 s)
   App 4f007f1: sunset 08-13 11:36:42 (-0.2 min); Sun wholly covered 18:26:23 .. 21:03:25 (+0 s, +4 s)

F. The two flagship windows with the app reading its bundled Horizons tables (as in the browser; sections A-D ran its model)
   Independent: Blue Ghost last limb 19:30:03, Sun wholly covered 06:17:24 .. 08:34:25; IM-2 Sun wholly covered 05:33:04 .. 08:18:52, Earthset 03-19 04:07:45, sunset 03-19 23:17:13
   App 375f816 (horizons): Blue Ghost last limb 19:30:11 (+8 s), covered 06:17:26 .. 08:34:26 (+2 s, +1 s); IM-2 covered 05:33:05 .. 08:18:52 (+0 s, -0 s), Earthset 03-19 04:11:31 (+3.8 min), sunset 03-19 23:17:27 (+0.2 min)
   App 4f007f1 (horizons): Blue Ghost last limb 19:30:04 (+1 s), covered 06:17:26 .. 08:34:26 (+2 s, +1 s); IM-2 covered 05:33:05 .. 08:18:52 (+0 s, -0 s), Earthset 03-19 04:09:38 (+1.9 min), sunset 03-19 23:17:08 (-0.1 min)
   At IM-2 Earth sinks by about 0.05 deg per hour and the Sun by less, so one minute there is under 0.001 deg.

E. Apollo 11-17: Sun and Earth altitude/azimuth at 43 documented instants (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal table by J. Scotti, values to 0.01 deg)
   worst difference over the 43 instants, deg (altitude / azimuth arc):
     app 375f816 skyAt minus published:            Sun 0.065 / 0.400   Earth 0.261 / 0.046
     app 375f816 skyAt minus SPICE at the site:     Sun 0.0021 / 0.0033 Earth 0.0019 / 0.0034
     app 4f007f1 skyAt minus published:            Sun 0.065 / 0.400   Earth 0.261 / 0.046
     app 4f007f1 skyAt minus SPICE at the site:     Sun 0.0021 / 0.0033 Earth 0.0019 / 0.0034
     SPICE at the site minus published:               Sun 0.066 / 0.403   Earth 0.261 / 0.044
     SPICE from the Moon's centre minus published:    Sun 0.067 / 0.403   Earth 0.075 / 0.044   (the table's own method)
   The table is built from sub-Earth and sub-solar points, i.e. from the Moon's centre, so its Earth altitudes lack the site parallax.
